# `canair pids`

```
usage: canair pids [-h]
                   {upsert-param,rename-param,rm-param,rename-pid,rm-pid,add-pid,add-research,set-status,rm-research,set-research-notes,set-research-result,set-pid-status,set-pid-variable-length,set-support-map,set-pid-period,set-response-frames,set-pid-notes,set-pid-source,set-pid-source-links,hoist-provenance,set-identity,rm-identity,set-can-bus,set-iocontrol-ranges,set-iocontrol,set-wake,set-addressing}
                   ...

[UDS] Safely edit ecus/ parameters and research entries (domain A — diagnostic UDS PIDs, freeform WiCAN expressions). The broadcast-frame (domain B) authoring counterpart is `canair signals` (linear signals/ maps).

positional arguments:
  {upsert-param,rename-param,rm-param,rename-pid,rm-pid,add-pid,add-research,set-status,rm-research,set-research-notes,set-research-result,set-pid-status,set-pid-variable-length,set-support-map,set-pid-period,set-response-frames,set-pid-notes,set-pid-source,set-pid-source-links,hoist-provenance,set-identity,rm-identity,set-can-bus,set-iocontrol-ranges,set-iocontrol,set-wake,set-addressing}
    upsert-param        Add or update a signal
    rename-param        Rename a signal (key only; fields preserved)
    rm-param            Remove a signal
    rename-pid          Rename a PID key (e.g. B002 -> 22B002)
    rm-pid              Remove a whole PID (header, status, parameters)
    add-pid             Create a new parameter-less PID (discovery/identity
                        placeholder)
    add-research        Append a research: entry
    set-status          Update a research item's status
    rm-research         Remove a research: item
    set-research-notes  Set (or clear) a research item's free-text notes
    set-research-result
                        Set (or clear) a research item's short result summary
    set-pid-status      Set a PID's lifecycle status
    set-pid-variable-length
                        Flag a PID as returning legitimately variable-length
                        responses
    set-support-map     Declare where a PID's support map sits (which
                        following bits/bytes are signals)
    set-pid-period      Set how often the WiCAN AutoPID re-polls a PID (ms)
    set-response-frames
                        Set how many CAN frames a PID's response occupies
                        (skips the adapter's wait)
    set-pid-notes       Set (or clear) a PID's free-text notes
    set-pid-source      Set (or clear) the source every parameter of a PID
                        inherits
    set-pid-source-links
                        Set (or clear) the source links every parameter of a
                        PID inherits
    hoist-provenance    Move source/source_links repeated on a PID's
                        parameters up to the PID
    set-identity        Set a curated identity field (e.g. notes)
    rm-identity         Remove an identity field from an ECU
    set-can-bus         Set the physical CAN bus segment(s) the ECU sits on
    set-iocontrol-ranges
                        Set the IOControl (0x2F) scan DID ranges swept on this
                        ECU
    set-iocontrol       Set fields of a curated IOControl actuator entry
    set-wake            Set how to rouse a fast-sleeping ECU before reads
                        (wake ritual)
    set-addressing      Set an ECU's CAN addressing override (mode / extension
                        bytes / FC id / rx_id)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

  # Record a decoded parameter
  canair pids upsert-param MCU 2102 MCU_MOTOR_TORQUE "[S12:S13]/100" \
      --unit Nm --min -300 --max 300 --unverified --source "Soul VMCU CSV" \
      --notes "signed 16-bit BE at B12:B13"

  # Track a new investigation, then close it out
  canair pids add-research MCU --type decode --target 2103 \
      --status captured --priority P2 --prereq charging --notes "27 bytes, zeros"
  canair pids set-status MCU 2103 done --type decode

  # Set an ECU's curated identity notes (comment/format-preserving)
  canair pids set-identity BMS notes "Battery Management System — see sessions:."
```

## `canair pids set-support-map`

```
usage: canair pids set-support-map [-h] [--at AT] [--length LENGTH]
                                   [--unit {bit,byte}] [--clear] [--dir DIR]
                                   [--no-validate]
                                   ecu pid

Record that the PID's data starts with a constant support map: LENGTH bytes at
data offset AT (counted after the SID and DID echo) marking which of the data
that follows are real signals, one map bit per data bit (--unit bit) or per
data byte (--unit byte), most significant bit first. `canair investigate ECU
--support-map` finds and scores candidates and prints the exact command;
`canair coverage` then stops reporting bits the map does not mark. --clear
removes the declaration.

positional arguments:
  ecu
  pid

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --at AT            Data offset of the first map byte (usually 0)
  --length LENGTH    Map length in bytes (1-4)
  --unit {bit,byte}  What one map bit marks
  --clear            Remove the declaration
  --dir DIR          ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate      Skip the post-edit schema validation gate
```

## `canair pids set-pid-period`

```
usage: canair pids set-pid-period [-h] [--dir DIR] [--no-validate]
                                  ecu pid MS|clear

Set the PID's AutoPID polling interval in milliseconds. It applies only to the
profile shipped to the device (`wican autopid write`); `monitor` and `read`
poll every selector once per cycle regardless. 0 is refused because the
firmware treats it as unset and substitutes a default.

positional arguments:
  ecu
  pid
  MS|clear       interval in milliseconds (int >= 1), or 'clear' to remove it
                 (device default 5000)

options:

  --dir DIR      ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate  Skip the post-edit schema validation gate
```

## `canair pids hoist-provenance`

```
usage: canair pids hoist-provenance [-h] [--dry-run] [--dir DIR]
                                    [--no-validate]
                                    [ecu] [pid]

Find PIDs whose parameters repeat the same source or source_links and state
the value once on the PID instead. A field moves only when it changes no
signal's provenance: every parameter must carry its own non-empty value, and
at least two share the most common one (a differing parameter keeps its value
as an override). The result is verified before it is kept. Name an ECU (and
PID) to narrow the sweep; with neither, the whole profile is processed. --dry-
run lists what would move.

positional arguments:
  ecu            Limit to this ECU (default: every ECU)
  pid            Limit to this PID

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --dry-run      List what would move; write nothing
  --dir DIR      ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate  Skip the post-edit schema validation gate
```

range.

## `canair pids set-iocontrol`

```
usage: canair pids set-iocontrol [-h] [--label LABEL] [--notes NOTES]
                                 [--verified | --no-verified] [--on HEX]
                                 [--off HEX] [--release HEX]
                                 [--session | --no-session]
                                 [--session-mode XX] [--hold | --no-hold]
                                 [--status-param NAME] [--dir DIR]
                                 [--no-validate]
                                 ecu DID

Set fields of an existing iocontrol: entry (the actuators `canair io` drives). Writes only the fields given, adding any the entry lacks. Promote a scanner discovery first (the `canair io` TUI's P key).

positional arguments:
  ecu
  DID                   The iocontrol: entry key (e.g. BC01)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL
  --notes NOTES         Free-text note (replaces the existing one)
  --verified, --no-verified
                        Mark as tested on this car (--no-verified to clear)
  --on HEX              Full ON request (e.g. 2FBC0103)
  --off HEX             Full OFF request (e.g. 2FBC0100)
  --release HEX         Full request that hands the output back to the ECU,
                        sent on exit, on Ctrl+C and by --poll. UDS implies
                        2F{DID}00; a KWP2000 0x30 entry has no standard one,
                        and `canair io` refuses its ON until this is set
  --session, --no-session
                        Open a diagnostic session before actuating
  --session-mode XX     DiagnosticSessionControl sub-function to open (default
                        03; an OEM session such as Nissan C0 also needs the
                        profile quirk that permits it)
  --hold, --no-hold     Keep the session alive after ON until Ctrl+C, then
                        send the release
  --status-param NAME   Signal read before and after actuating, as a best-
                        effort readback
  --dir DIR             ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate         Skip the post-edit schema validation gate

examples:
  canair pids set-iocontrol IGPM BC01 --verified --label 'Low beam'
  canair pids set-iocontrol BCM 6900 --session-mode C0 --no-hold
  canair pids set-iocontrol HVAC F010 --on 2FF01003FF --off 2FF01000
  canair pids set-iocontrol BCM 6900 --release 30690000
```

## `canair pids set-wake`

```
usage: canair pids set-wake [-h] --method {rapid_read,session,relay}
                            [--prime-pid REQ] [--attempts N]
                            [--interval-ms MS] [--sleep-timer-ms MS]
                            [--session-mode XX] [--notes NOTES] [--dir DIR]
                            [--no-validate]
                            ecu

Declare a per-ECU wake ritual (canlib.wake). Some modules (e.g. a Smart Key
Module) power their CAN transceiver only briefly and sleep again within a
second or two, so a single 10 01 wake races the sleep timer. `rapid_read`
fires a cheap prime PID back-to-back to hold the transceiver awake, then opens
a session — honoured by `session <ECU> --wake` on both transports.

positional arguments:
  ecu

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --method {rapid_read,session,relay}
                        rapid_read = back-to-back primes (fast-sleepers);
                        session = single 10 01; relay = rapid_read + iocontrol
                        relay (Ioniq SKM, needs skm_wakeup quirk)
  --prime-pid REQ       Cheap full UDS request fired repeatedly to hold the
                        ECU awake (SID-first, e.g. 22B003 / 1001 / 3E00;
                        default 1001)
  --attempts N          Back-to-back prime frames (default 6)
  --interval-ms MS      Gap between primes in ms — must be under the ECU's
                        sleep timer (default 60)
  --sleep-timer-ms MS   Documented time the ECU stays awake after a frame
                        (informational)
  --session-mode XX     DiagnosticSessionControl sub-function entered after
                        waking (default 03)
  --notes NOTES         Free-text note on the wake ritual
  --dir DIR             ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate         Skip the post-edit schema validation gate
```

## `canair pids set-addressing`

```
usage: canair pids set-addressing [-h] [--mode MODE]
                                  [--target-address TARGET_ADDRESS]
                                  [--source-address SOURCE_ADDRESS]
                                  [--fc-id FC_ID] [--rx-id RX_ID] [--dir DIR]
                                  [--no-validate]
                                  ecu

Set the make-specific CAN addressing knobs on an ECU: the addressing `mode` (11-bit vs the 29-bit modes / extended-11-bit), the ISO-TP extension bytes (`target_address`/`source_address`, for BMW/PSA extended-11-bit), a flow-control arbitration override (`fc_id`, for functional-TX / physical-RX ECUs like Renault/Mitsubishi), and/or the response-address `rx_id`. Writes only the fields given.

positional arguments:
  ecu

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode MODE           Addressing mode (normal_11bit | normal_29bit |
                        normal_fixed_29bit | normal_extended_11bit |
                        extended_29bit)
  --target-address TARGET_ADDRESS
                        ISO-TP target extension byte (hex, e.g. 0x12) —
                        extended-11-bit/29-bit modes
  --source-address SOURCE_ADDRESS
                        ISO-TP tester (source) byte (hex, default 0xF1) —
                        extended-11-bit modes
  --fc-id FC_ID         Flow-control arbitration override (hex) — functional-
                        TX / physical-RX ECUs
  --rx-id RX_ID         CAN response-address override (hex, e.g. 0x784)
  --dir DIR             ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate         Skip the post-edit schema validation gate

examples:
  canair pids set-addressing PCM --mode normal_fixed_29bit
  canair pids set-addressing DME --mode normal_extended_11bit --target-address 0x12
  canair pids set-addressing EVC --mode normal_29bit --fc-id 0x18DADBF1
  canair pids set-addressing BMS --rx-id 0x784
```
